chapters.name: General-Purpose Financial Statements
chapters.summary: How businesses present the balance sheet, income statement, comprehensive income, changes in equity, cash flows, and notes.
keyPoints: Classify cash flows as operating, investing, or financing.
Know what goes in other comprehensive income.
Separate current and noncurrent items on the balance sheet.

chapters.name: Not-for-Profit Entities
chapters.summary: How not-for-profit entities report net assets, contributions, expenses, and cash flows.
keyPoints: Net assets are with or without donor restrictions.
Conditional promises are not recognized until the conditions are met.
Expenses are reported by function and nature.

chapters.name: State and Local Governments
chapters.summary: Foundational concepts of state and local government reporting: funds, measurement focus, basis of accounting, and government-wide statements.
keyPoints: Governmental funds use the modified accrual basis.
Government-wide statements use the economic resources focus and full accrual.
Know the reconciling items between fund and government-wide statements.

chapters.name: Cash, Receivables, and Investments
chapters.summary: Cash and bank reconciliations, receivables and credit losses, and investments in debt and equity securities.
keyPoints: Debt securities are held-to-maturity, available-for-sale, or trading.
Equity securities are generally measured at fair value through net income.
Credit losses use an expected-loss allowance.

chapters.name: Inventory, PP&E, and Intangibles
chapters.summary: Inventory cost flows and valuation, property and equipment costs, depreciation and impairment, and intangible assets.
keyPoints: FIFO and average cost inventory use lower of cost and net realizable value.
Capitalize costs needed to get an asset ready for use.
Goodwill is tested for impairment, not amortized, for public companies.

chapters.name: Payables, Debt, and Equity
chapters.summary: Accrued liabilities, bonds and notes payable, debt classification and extinguishment, and equity transactions.
keyPoints: Bond interest expense uses the effective interest method.
Treasury stock under the cost method reduces equity.
Stock dividends move amounts within equity.

chapters.name: Revenue Recognition and Leases
chapters.summary: The five-step revenue model and lessee accounting for finance and operating leases.
keyPoints: Follow the five steps: contract, obligations, price, allocation, recognition.
Allocate the price by standalone selling prices.
A lessee records a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for both lease types.

chapters.name: Accounting Changes, Income Taxes, and Other Transactions
chapters.summary: Accounting changes and error corrections, contingencies, income taxes, fair value measurement, and subsequent events.
keyPoints: Changes in estimate are prospective; errors are restated.
Deferred taxes come from temporary differences at enacted rates.
Recognized subsequent events give evidence about conditions at the balance sheet date.
